'''Oscar Marín Parra''' [[FMedSci]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 31 March 1971) is a Spanish and British [[neuroscientist]]. He is married to neuroscientist [[Beatriz Rico (neuroscientist)|Beatriz Rico]].

==Education==
Oscar Marín was born in [[Madrid]] and received his undergraduate degree in [[Biology]] from [[Complutense University of Madrid|Universidad Complutense de Madrid]], and later his PhD in neuroscience. He then undertook postdoctoral training with [[María Ángela Nieto]] at the [[Cajal Institute|Instituto Cajal]] and John L. Rubenstein and [[Marc Tessier-Lavigne]] at the [[University of California, San Francisco|University of California in San Francisco]].

==Research and career==
Before being appointed Professor of [[Neuroscience]] at [[King's College London]] in 2014, Marín started his career at the Instituto de Neurociencias in Alicante (Spain) between 2003 and 2014. He has directed the Centre for Developmental Neurobiology at King's since 2014,<ref>{{Cite web |title=CDN - organisation |url=https://devneuro.org/cdn/organisation.php |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=devneuro.org}}</ref> and the MRC Centre for Neurodevelopmental Disorders since 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Team – CNDD |url=https://devneuro.org/cndd/about.php |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=devneuro.org}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 2004, Marín received the European Young Investigator Award (EURYI) in its first round.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://archives.esf.org/coordinating-research/euryi/awards/2004.html | title=2004 : European Science Foundation }}</ref> In 2011 he received the [[Rey Jaime I Awards|Rey Jaime I Award]] and in 2012 the FENS-EJN Young Investigator Award. In 2014 Marín received the Roger de Spoelberch Award for his work on the neurobiology of schizophrenia. In 2017 Marín received the Ramón y Cajal Medal from the Spanish Royal Academy of Sciences, and the Remedios Caro Almela Award in 2019. In 2023, he received the [[European College of Neuropsychopharmacology|ECNP]] Neuropsychopharmacology Award in Basic Science Research and in 2024, Marín was awarded the prestigious FENS-EJN Prize.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CDN |url=https://devneuro.org/cdn/news-detail.php?NewsID=478&type=91 |access-date=2024-11-01 |website=devneuro.org}}</ref>

Marín was elected a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO) in 2010, and a member of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-13 |title=50 leading biomedical and health scientists elected to the prestigious Academy Fellowship |url=https://acmedsci.ac.uk/more/news/50-leading-biomedical-and-health-scientists-elected-to-the-prestigious-academy-fellowship |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=Academy of Medical Sciences}}</ref> In 2022 he was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://english.elpais.com/science-tech/2022-07-15/changing-small-pieces-of-the-cerebral-cortex-can-generate-superhero-abilities-oscar-marin-neuroscientist.html | title='Changing small pieces of the cerebral cortex can generate superhero abilities': Óscar Marín, neuroscientist | date=15 July 2022 }}</ref> Marín was a founding member of the [[European Research Council]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Scientific Council of the European Research\nCouncil announced |url=https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_05_956 |access-date=2025-05-14 |website=European Commission - European Commission}}</ref>
